title: AMD MI400 GPU at Hot Chips 2026
gist: AMD detailed the Instinct MI455X: eight N2 accelerator complex dies with N3P fabric, cache and I/O dies on CoWoS-L, 256 active work group processors, 192 MB of global L2, and 12 HBM4 stacks totaling 432GB at 23.3 TB/s. Headline gains are 40.26 petaflops MXFP4 (up to 4x MI355X) and roughly 2.9x total HBM bandwidth, paired with a ROCm push that ships AI Skills so coding agents become ROCm users.

insights.claim: The MI455X is a modular chiplet design built from eight accelerator complex dies on N2 flanked by fabric, cache, and I/O dies on N3P, packaging 256 total active work group processors with 192 MB of global L2 and 12 HBM4 stacks running 432GB at 23.3 TB/s.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: AMD is an early N2 volume customer for compute dies, which bears on TSMC 2nm ramp allocation and on AMD's cost per accelerator.
insights.quote: It packages 256 total active work group processors with 192 MB of global L2 and 12x HBM4 stacks running 432GB at 23.3 TB/s
insights.locator: At the center of the tray is the AMD Instinct MI455X

insights.claim: AMD assigns each die type to the node that best fits its job, with compute dies on N2 under 3D hybrid-bonded XCDs for higher density per watt while N3P fabric, cache, and I/O dies plus CoWoS-L packaging tie the package around twelve HBM4 stacks.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Node-mixing lets AMD limit expensive N2 area to compute, a cost advantage over monolithic leading-edge designs.
insights.quote: This packaging split is notable because each die type moves to the node that best fits its job.
insights.locator: This packaging split is notable

insights.claim: One of the challenges with the MI455X packaging approach is ensuring power delivery to all of the dies as well as cooling them.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Power delivery and thermals, not transistor count, are the practical limits on how far chiplet-stacked accelerators can scale.
insights.quote: One of the challenges with this approach is ensuring you can get power to all of the ties as well as just cooling them.
insights.locator: AMD has its conceptual block diagram

insights.claim: The MI455X connects through PCIe Gen 6 as well as 72 UALoE lanes pushing 3.6 TB/s.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: 3.6 TB/s of scale-up per GPU is the number that must be compared against NVLink 6's 3.6 TB/s all-to-all claim on the same axis.
insights.locator: At the center of the tray is the AMD Instinct MI455X

themes.theme: Memory and cache hierarchy gains over MI355X

insights.claim: Main memory jumps from 288 GB of HBM3E on MI355X to 432 GB of HBM4 on MI455X, a 1.5x capacity increase, while AMD lists roughly 2.9x the total HBM bandwidth.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Bandwidth rising nearly 2x faster than capacity signals AMD is targeting decode-bound serving, where bandwidth sets tokens per second.
insights.quote: Main memory jumps from 288 GB of HBM3E to 432 GB of HBM4, a 1.5x capacity increase, while AMD lists roughly 2.9x the total HBM bandwidth.
insights.locator: The new MI455X substantially expands the on-chip memory hierarchy

insights.claim: AMD doubles per-SIMD vector registers and per-WGP local data share, and a 4 MB L2 broadcast arbitrator can amplify bandwidth by up to 4x.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Bandwidth amplification in cache is cheaper than adding HBM stacks, and it is where AMD says the SoC was re-architected.
insights.locator: The new MI455X substantially expands the on-chip memory hierarchy

insights.claim: Peak MXFP4 compute reaches 40.26 petaflops, up to 4x MI355X, with MXFP6 and MXFP8 each at 20.13 petaflops and vector FP16 plus matrix or vector FP32 reaching 315 TF on a 256 WGP architecture.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: The 4x headline comes from narrower precision rather than transistor scaling, so realized gains depend on models running at 4-bit.
insights.quote: the headline is a peak MXFP4 figure of 40.26 petaflops, up to 4x the MI355X
insights.locator: On the compute side

insights.claim: Four-bit tensor LUT instructions let data stay in 4-bit memory and convert to 4, 6, or 8-bit compute formats, with shared-scale blocks that can span 16 or 32 elements and a new fractional scale for MXFP4.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Keeping weights in 4-bit while computing at higher precision doubles effective memory capacity, a direct answer to HBM scarcity.
insights.locator: AMD walks through the MX data formats

insights.claim: Native Wave32 execution and a new transcendental engine target lower dispatch latency and faster attention math.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Attention-specific hardware mirrors NVIDIA's approach, showing convergence on where inference bottlenecks actually sit.
insights.locator: On the compute side

themes.theme: Keeping data in place and off the compute path

insights.claim: A Tensor Data Mover copies data asynchronously into local LDS without staging through registers, while work group clusters and L2 multicast cut redundant traffic for operators like GEMM and Flash Attention.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Data-movement elimination is the efficiency lever both AMD and NVIDIA are pulling this generation, more so than raw FLOPS.
insights.locator: This efficiency push is about keeping work and data in place

insights.claim: AMD moves data movement into dedicated DMA engines so transfers run in parallel with AI kernels instead of stealing compute cycles, with topology-aware HBM DMA automatically affinitizing traffic to UALoE links.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Keeping software oblivious to data placement across 72 GPUs lowers the porting burden, one of the main frictions in leaving CUDA.
insights.quote: which keeps software oblivious to data placement and spreads load across the 72-GPU fabric
insights.locator: AMD moves data movement into dedicated DMA engines

insights.claim: A reworked command processor lowers dispatch latency so short kernels stay fed.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Short-kernel efficiency matters disproportionately for agentic workloads composed of many small operations.
insights.locator: This efficiency push is about keeping work and data in place

themes.theme: ROCm and closing the CUDA gap

insights.claim: AMD is shipping AI Skills so popular coding agents such as Claude, Codex, Cursor, and Gemini become ROCm users, positioning the ROCm core framework as the integration point.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Using coding agents as the porting workforce is a novel and cheap route around the CUDA software moat, worth tracking for effectiveness.
insights.quote: It positions the ROCm core framework as the integration point and is shipping AI Skills so popular agents such as Claude, Codex, Cursor, and Gemini become ROCm users
insights.locator: Software is where AMD is trying to narrow the ROCm gap

insights.claim: AMD adds a Hyperloom tool for end-to-end workload optimization alongside the ROCm core framework.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Tooling breadth is the practical measure of whether ROCm can support production deployments beyond hand-tuned benchmarks.
insights.locator: Software is where AMD is trying to narrow the ROCm gap

insights.claim: The through-line of AMD's presentation is pairing a substantially larger memory and compute envelope in the MI455X with the Helios rack fabric and a software stack designed to ease the CUDA migration.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: AMD's competitive theory is hardware parity plus migration cost reduction, so migration friction is the variable that determines share gains.
insights.quote: AMD pairs a substantially larger memory and compute envelope in the MI455X with the Helios rack fabric and a software stack designed to ease the CUDA migration.
insights.locator: It is a dense presentation

insights.claim: AMD reports 20 TB/s of measured MLA decode bandwidth in FP8 for 3.8x higher performance, 20 petaflops of measured FP4 compute for 3.3x higher AI compute, 3.2 TB/s of scale-up bandwidth for 3.5x, and 190 GB/s of scale-out bandwidth for 2x versus MI355X.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Measured rather than peak figures make these the numbers to hold AMD to when third-party benchmarks appear.
insights.quote: It reports 20 TB/s of measured MLA decode bandwidth in FP8 for 3.8x higher performance, 20 petaflops of measured FP4 compute for 3.3x higher AI compute
insights.locator: AMD closes the architecture section with ROCm.AI performance comparisons

insights.claim: AMD estimates a 2.4x gain in AI energy efficiency with the MI455X on the way to its 2030 goal of a 20x improvement in rack-scale efficiency.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: A public 20x-by-2030 rack efficiency target is a measurable commitment against which AMD's generational execution can be scored.
insights.quote: AMD also estimates a 2.4x gain in AI energy efficiency on the way to its 2030 goal of a 20x improvement in rack-scale efficiency.
insights.locator: AMD closes the architecture section with ROCm.AI performance comparisons

insights.claim: AMD's scale curve runs from the roughly 65 million parameter Transformer in 2017 through GPT-4 class models around a trillion parameters in 2023 to the 10 trillion-plus agentic and reasoning models AMD expects this year.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: A 10x parameter jump expected within a single year is the demand assumption underpinning AMD's memory-capacity investment.
insights.quote: on to the 10 trillion-plus agentic and reasoning models AMD expects this year
insights.locator: AMD opens with the argument that AI work is broadening

insights.claim: AMD argues AI work is broadening from single-model training into a mix of frontier training, enterprise fine-tuning, and always-on inference, with the takeaway that infrastructure has to move data as fast as models scale.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: A broadening workload mix favors flexible accelerators over training-optimized ones and supports the always-on inference demand case.
insights.locator: AMD opens with the argument that AI work is broadening

insights.claim: Each Helios compute tray holds four MI455X EAMs fed by a single-socket AMD EPYC 9006 SP7 server CPU over Infinity Fabric, with UALoE links carrying scale-up traffic at 1.8 TB/s per direction per GPU and up to three Pensando Vulcano 800 AI NICs per EAM.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Up to three 800G NICs per GPU sets the per-accelerator networking attach rate driving AMD's Pensando revenue.
insights.locator: This basic building block is a compute tray
